title: The Protocol of Station Meridian
premise: When gravity fails for nine seconds across the Meridian system, memory-smuggler Lior Voss discovers the flicker was a countdown: an ancient jump engine buried in Station Meridian is waking, and both the Concord and the Freehold fleets believe the other side activated it. Lior, the only person carrying a smuggled memory-recording that proves a third party — a dead AI cult — triggered it, must decide whether to reveal the truth and expose her own crimes, or let the fleets destroy each other. Falling in love with Concord investigator Sefa Idris, who is hunting the same memory, she builds a fragile lie that keeps both fleets at bay while she races to the station's core. In the end she broadcasts the truth and her own confession together, sacrificing her freedom to close the jump window, and walks out of the wreckage into a system that must now judge everyone — including her.
about_author: Cyrus Delacroix is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests between shifts and now writes science fiction about the people the manifests never mention. They live near a spaceport and claim to judge cities by the quality of their night-shift diners.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Mid-run through Meridian's contested customs corridor, gravity dies for nine seconds; cargo, crew, and a sealed memory-shard she shouldn't have float weightless. When it returns, every comm channel screams. Emotional beat: a veteran smuggler realizing her routine life just ended.

chapters.title: Contraband and Consequence
chapters.summary: Lior docks at Station Meridian's underbelly, where her fence, Ombra, reveals the shard she's carrying is a fragment of the jump engine's activation log — worth fleets, worth killing for. Emotional beat: greed curdling into fear as she understands what she's holding.

chapters.title: The Investigator
chapters.summary: Sefa Idris's POV. A Concord truth-officer arrives on the station hunting the memory-shard, interrogating smugglers with unsettling gentleness. He interviews Lior and, suspiciously, lets her go. Emotional beat: two liars recognizing each other across a table.

chapters.title: Fleet Shadows
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Concord and Freehold warships take mirror positions around Meridian, each blaming the other for the gravity event. The station's neutral charter strains. Emotional beat: the claustrophobia of being small between two giants.

chapters.title: What the Shard Remembers
chapters.summary: Lior finally plays the shard: a dying cultist's memory of the Choir of the Deep Signal, a machine-worship cult, manually waking the jump engine. POV alternates between Lior present and the memory's first person. Emotional beat: awe and horror — someone else started this war.

chapters.title: A Lie With Two Audiences
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. To buy time, she sends the Concord a forged fragment implying Freehold involvement — and vice versa — keeping both fleets suspicious rather than certain. Emotional beat: the intoxicating, terrible power of being the only person who knows the truth.

chapters.title: Ombra's Price
chapters.summary: Ombra, threatened by both fleets' agents, sells a partial description of Lior to the Freehold. Lior must abandon her ship and identity, moving into the station's forgotten levels. Emotional beat: betrayal by the only family she had.

chapters.title: The Forgotten Levels
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with Sefa interludes. Hiding among station ghosts — stateless dockworkers, ex-cultists — Lior meets a former Choir member who confirms the engine can be shut down from the core, but only before the jump window opens. Emotional beat: finding unexpected community among the discarded.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Sefa finds Lior — not to arrest her, but because his own investigation has reached the same dead end: his superiors want a culprit, not a truth. Over stolen wine they compare notes. Emotional beat: love beginning as conspiracy, two people choosing each other over their institutions.

chapters.title: The Window Opens
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The jump engine's window begins forming; gravity flickers again, longer. Both fleets go to alert readiness. The station's council begs Lior, now half-legend, to do something. Emotional beat: a private lie becoming a public burden.

chapters.title: Sefa's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. His Concord handlers order him to extract Lior and the shard by force, disavowing the investigation. He must choose: his career and duty, or Lior and the truth. Emotional beat: duty revealed as just another loyalty, and loyalties can be re-chosen.

chapters.title: The Freehold Offer
chapters.summary: Freehold agents capture Lior and offer her amnesty and riches for the shard — and for testifying that Concord did it. She stalls, learning the Freehold's evidence is forged by someone inside the Choir's remnants. Emotional beat: discovering the conspiracy is still alive and still steering.

chapters.title: Ghost Signal
chapters.summary: Lior escapes during a station blackout with the ex-cultist's help, tracing the Choir's surviving node to a sealed habitat ring. Emotional beat: terror giving way to grim competence — the smuggler finally running her best route.

chapters.title: The Choir Remnant
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She finds the surviving Choir cell preparing to complete the jump — believing ascension through the engine is salvation, and that a fleet war is an acceptable offering. Emotional beat: confronting believers who make her liar's pragmatism look like honesty.

chapters.title: What Lior Voss Did
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, interrogated by his own side, confesses his compromise of the investigation to protect Lior. Stripped of rank, he goes rogue, carrying the only copy of her forged fragments — evidence that could damn her. Emotional beat: love as an act of self-destruction.

chapters.title: The Core
chapters.summary: Lior infiltrates the jump engine's core with the ex-cultist as guide. She finds the shutdown interface — and discovers shutting it down requires a full, unedited memory broadcast from someone who witnessed the activation: her shard, and her confession of the forgeries. Emotional beat: the trap of her own lie closing around her.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Both fleets move to final engagement positions as the window nears opening. Sefa reaches Lior by smuggler channels; they plan the broadcast knowing it ends her freedom and his career. Emotional beat: a quiet, terrified vow between two people about to burn their lives down.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Lior hijacks the station's master array and transmits everything — the cultist's memory, the Choir's survival, her own forgeries — in one unbroken confession. The fleets stand down, stunned; the Choir cell is exposed and stormed. Emotional beat: liberation and devastation in the same breath.

chapters.title: Closing the Window
chapters.summary: Lior and Sefa enter the shutdown sequence as the window strains open, the Choir's last loyalist sabotaging the attempt. The engine dies with seconds to spare, and gravity across the system steadies — permanently. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, and grief for the lives they were.

chapters.title: Judgment
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Lior surrenders to a joint Concord–Freehold tribunal — the first either fleet has ever held together. Sefa, disgraced, testifies as her character witness, not her defender. Emotional beat: justice finally arriving from outside the law that failed everyone.

chapters.title: The Sentence
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The tribunal sentences her to service rebuilding the station's forgotten levels — neither prison nor pardon. Sefa chooses exile from Concord to stay with her. Emotional beat: a sentence that feels, impossibly, like a beginning.

chapters.title: Meridian, After
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Lior's POV. Months later, the station thrives under joint stewardship; the shard's truth is taught in its schools, Lior's confession included. On a gravity-steady dock, she and Sefa watch ships pass through safe, honest corridors. Emotional beat: peace earned, not granted — and a love that outlasted duty.
